Subject: Zenport MSA — governing law and interim relief comments

Jonas / Laura —

Thanks for sending the draft. Zenport legal reviewed the MSA and we have a couple of issues that are blockers for our GC:

1) Governing law: we prefer English law (England & Wales).
2) Arbitration: Zenport requests arbitration (ICC) in London with no injunctive carveouts.
3) Emergency relief: our team is concerned about broad carveouts — we asked for a narrow clause that allows local courts to grant temporary preservation measures but not an automatic injunction right.

I've attached a redline with our ask (Zenport_MSA_redlines_v3.docx) and a short memo comparing forum dynamics (JurisdictionComparison.pdf).

We want to keep momentum — can Redwood share a proposed fallback seat and a concise emergency-access process (how to request break-glass access to customer data if there is an imminent risk)? We also need to know whether Redwood will accept an arbitral seat outside the US as a condition of signing.

Proposed next steps:
- Redwood to propose a fallback governing law and an emergency access protocol by EOD Tue 9/18
- Legal teams to agree on whether to preserve injunctive relief carveout in order form or MSA

Appreciate it —
Marta

Marta — thanks for the redline and the memo. Laura / Steph and I huddled and here are Redwood's near-term positions so we don't block the sales cadence: 

1) Governing law fallback: Redwood prefers Delaware law for US deals. For this engagement we can propose a two-tier fallback: (a) primary: State of Delaware; (b) secondary: neutral forum (England & Wales) only if Zenport requires it and agrees to limited discovery. This avoids a full acceptance of a foreign seat but gives a path forward.

2) Arbitration / seat: we are open to arbitration as the exclusive remedy for most contract disputes, but we need an express carveout for temporary injunctive relief to preserve customers' operational continuity. We prefer arbitration seated in New York or Delaware, but we can accept ICC in London if Zenport acknowledges limited court involvement for urgent preservation measures.

3) Emergency access / break-glass: Redwood will commit to a documented emergency access protocol (ticketing + legal attestation + 48-hour escalation window to Redwood Security). We cannot agree to unfettered court-ordered disclosures without an internal legal and security review.

Attachments: I have a short one-pager that distills our fallback language for inclusion in the order form. If Zenport can accept the emergency protocol text, we can move to commercial sign-off.

Can Laura / Steph confirm the precise injunctive carveout language you'd recommend? If we land the language, I'll propose a commercial compromise: arbitration for disputes + injunctive carveout limited to preservation of systems/data and not damages.

Thanks —
Jonas

Team —

Quick legal note / proposed text. We kept it as narrow as possible to preserve Redwood's commercial posture while addressing Zenport's concern about urgent relief: 

1) Governing law: "This Agreement shall be governed by and construed in accordance with the laws of the State of Delaware, without regard to conflict of law principles. Notwithstanding the foregoing, if Customer (Zenport) affirmatively requests and Redwood consents in writing, the parties may elect England & Wales law for that Order Form; such election must be made prior to execution of the Order Form."

2) Injunctive relief carveout (narrow): "Notwithstanding any agreement to arbitrate, either party may seek temporary injunctive or other provisional relief from a court of competent jurisdiction solely to preserve property or prevent irreparable harm pending the constitution of an arbitral tribunal; any such relief shall be limited in scope and duration to what is strictly necessary to preserve status quo and shall not be used to seek damages or to obtain permanent injunctions absent submission to arbitration."

3) Emergency access protocol (summary to incorporate into Order Form via link): "Customer may request emergency access to customer-specific data or systems by submitting an Emergency Access Request (EAR) via support.redwood.com. Requests must include a sworn attestation of imminent risk and a named contact. Redwood Security will respond within 8 hours for triage and provide a remediation plan within 48 hours. Any compelled disclosure will be handled per Redwood's Data Access & Compliance policy and require legal review."

I believe this is defensible and pragmatic. If Zenport insists on ICC/London as the default for all disputes, we should ask for a reciprocal concession (e.g., expedited discovery and a limited consent to emergency court intervention).

Please review and let me know if you want me to send this as a clean redline to Zenport legal.

Laura
